verdict.rationale: Auth0's own MFA docs list one-time passwords and recovery codes as supported factors and describe MFA as requiring more than one credential at login. Adaptive MFA (risk-based prompting) and Strong Customer Authentication for sensitive operations come close to step-up, but neither is explicitly documented as step-up enforcement. missing for 10: explicit confirmation that the OTP factor works with TOTP authenticator apps, documented step-up authentication enforcement for specific resources or actions, details on tenant-wide policy to require MFA, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can require multi-factor authentication with TOTP authenticator apps and backup codes, with step-up enforcement where needed

citations.quote: One-time passwords, WebAuthn with security keys, WebAuthn with device biometrics, Email notifications, Cisco Duo security, Recovery codes
MFA adds a layer of security during login that requires users to provide more than one credential to prove their digital identity.
Adaptive MFA: Only prompt users when a login seems risky, keeping security robust yet user-friendly.
Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) lets users review and approve sensitive operations in real time.
